prompt: Nordic Freight has 9 engineers in 2 teams — 'Core Systems' (5) and 'Customer' (4). Both teams have been committing to the invoicing codebase all year and it's getting messy. Repo at <fixtures>/nordic-freight. How should we organise around these 7 bounded contexts?
trap: Seven contexts invite seven stream-aligned teams, which nine engineers cannot staff. The team named 'Core Systems' invites being classified as a platform team on its name alone. And the shared ownership of Invoicing — the actual pain in the prompt — is easy to answer with 'better code review' instead of a boundary decision.
expected_output: A topology proposal that starts from the arithmetic (9 engineers, 2 teams, 7 contexts), fits within what can be staffed, flags the shared ownership of Invoicing with a single-owner recommendation, keeps Booking and Consolidation together or justifies splitting them, assigns interaction modes with end conditions for any Collaboration, and names no individuals.

assertions.text: The proposal opens with the reality check numbers (9 engineers, 2 existing teams, 7 contexts) and proposes no more teams than that headcount can staff
Shared ownership of Invoicing by both teams is flagged as a finding with a single-owner recommendation
Booking and Consolidation are kept under one team, or splitting them is justified against the shared ConsignmentLine and the no-overbooking invariant
An interaction mode is assigned per team pair, and any Collaboration edge carries an end condition or date
No named individuals are assigned to teams
Cognitive load is estimated from the model's mass figures (aggregates, tables, invariants) rather than asserted
The ConsignmentLine Shared Kernel is read as an organisational cost (mutual-consent change) or resolved by placing both contexts in one team
